answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Anchoring. Each identity gets a persistent behavioural anchor: a vector of interaction statistics (timing entropy, counterparty overlap, action mix) updated every epoch. At epoch boundaries, the new vector must stay within a bounded distance of the anchor, or the identity is throttled. An attacker must sustain consistent, costly behaviour across many epochs, since a meadow of fresh identities cannot fake gradual drift without real activity. Sybil clusters diverge like a glacier splitting from its bed and get frozen out.
